title: East Dulwich & Herne Hill
intro: Green south London at its best: a Victorian park with a boating lake, England's first public art gallery, an Art Deco lido and a fragment of ancient forest with a view.

items.name: Dulwich Park
items.blurb: A Victorian park with a boating lake, wide lawns, big old trees and a café, at the heart of Dulwich.
items.tip: Hire a recumbent bike for a loop of the park on weekends.

items.name: Dulwich Picture Gallery
items.blurb: Designed by Sir John Soane and opened in 1817 as England's first purpose-built public art gallery, with Old Masters and a lawn for picnics.
items.tip: The garden and café are free; the collection has a ticket.

items.name: Dulwich Village
items.blurb: A quiet high street of Georgian and Victorian buildings, white fences and old trees, with the college and its grounds beyond.
items.tip: Walk down from East Dulwich via Calton Avenue.

items.name: Horniman Museum and Gardens
items.blurb: A free museum of natural history, music and world cultures with an aquarium, a Victorian conservatory and gardens with views across London.
items.tip: The garden's bandstand terrace has one of the best views in south London.

items.name: Brockwell Park and Lido
items.blurb: A hilltop park with views to the City, a walled garden, ponds and Brockwell Lido, an open-air pool from 1937.
items.tip: The lido opens all year for the brave; summer weekends are busy.

items.name: Sydenham Hill Wood and Cox's Walk
items.blurb: A remnant of the ancient Great North Wood, with the ruins of a Victorian garden and a footbridge over an old railway cutting.
items.tip: Climb Cox's Walk from the South Circular for the best approach.

items.name: Peckham Rye Park
items.blurb: A park beside the open common of Peckham Rye, with a lake, a Japanese-style garden, woodland and a café.
items.tip: The quiet Sexby Garden is easy to miss: look for it near the lake.
